newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close weak on slow cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close weak on slow cash.

text.p: Reports of continued slow cash trade kept CME lumber futures pressured ahead of the U.S. Housing Starts report Tuesday, traders said.
Lumber closed $2.60 per tbf lower to $0.10 higher with May off $2.20 at $361.60 and July off most at $361.20.

The cash lumber market has remained slow and many traders kept to the sidelines ahead of the housing report. Although economists look for a rise in February starts from the previous months, lumber traders voiced caution on the report as demand for wood has not shown an increase that would go along with a rise in housing.
The average estimate on February housing starts was 1.45 million units versus 1.35 million the previous month. Economist estimates ranged from 1.35 to 1.50 million units.
